items.title: The future of Honkai Star Rail will be revealed on August 14th - teaser for update 4.5 presentation
items.content:
1 10 Aug 13:59 The creators of Honkai Star Rail are preparing to hold a presentation for the upcoming update 4.5, titled "Stakes in the City of a Thousand Stars." Such events by miHoYo (HoYoverse) are accompanied by the publication of promo codes for free gifts.

The Honkai Star Rail 4.5 stream is scheduled for August 14th (Friday), 2:30 PM Moscow time. The developers have already published a localized event poster.

The developers of Honkai Star Rail have published a brief announcement for the special stream. miHoYo plans to talk about the new features of version 4.5, and the broadcast "will take place" in Starfall City – among the invited stars will be Robin: Clearwing (an alternative version of the heroine):

This program will be held in the official streaming studio located in Starfall City. This summer version brings you a continuation of the Trailblaze Mission, with events unfolding shortly or long after the journey to Penacony. Let's spend the summer vacation together with Robin: Clearwing and Aventurine: Surf Rider! miHoYo (HoYoverse) The release of Honkai Star Rail 4.5 update is expected in late August of this year.

Philstar.com / EC Toledo MANILA, Philippines - What was once considered a niche interest has evolved into one of Southeast Asia's most influential consumer forces.

Across the region, gaming and anime communities are no longer just audiences for entertainment. They have become highly engaged consumer groups whose interests increasingly shape how brands design products, build experiences and connect with customers.

For Liam Cheng, regional marketing head of Southeast Asia & Middle East at Ugreen, this shift has fundamentally changed how technology brands approach collaborations with major entertainment franchises. Drawing from the company's latest partnership with HoYoverse for the Ugreen × Honkai: Star Rail collection, Cheng said fan communities today expect far more than traditional co-branding efforts.

"Gaming and anime communities have evolved from niche subcultures into a defining cultural force across Southeast Asia, and fan expectations have rightfully evolved right along with them," Cheng told Philstar.com in an interview.

The changing landscape became clear following Ugreen's earlier collaboration with Genshin Impac t. According to Cheng, the project revealed just how passionate gaming communities across Southeast Asia have become, both online and offline.

"When you create products that tie into characters, we've seen much stronger engagement across social discussions, user-generated content and purchase interest than with many traditional lifestyle or product-focused campaigns," he explained.

What stood out most, Cheng added, was that fans were not simply looking for products carrying the logo of a popular franchise. Instead, they expected collaborations to feel authentic to the source material while also serving a meaningful purpose in their everyday lives.

Those lessons directly informed Ugreen's approach to its latest collaboration with Honkai: Star Rail . Rather than focusing solely on collectibles, the company aimed to create practical technology accessories that incorporate visual elements and design assets from the video game while maintaining the brand's product functionality.

"The biggest challenge was finding the right balance between authenticity and practicality. We didn't want to create a product that was simply collectible. We wanted something fans would genuinely enjoy using every day," said Cheng.

Throughout the product development process, Ugreen worked closely with Honkai: Star Rail , combining the latter’s visual elements with their expertise in charging technology, craftsmanship and user experience.

The growing influence of fandom-driven consumer behavior also reflects a broader generational shift across Southeast Asia. Cheng noted that many people who grew up playing games and watching animated series have entered adulthood with significant purchasing power, bringing their interests with them into mainstream culture.

"From what we've observed, many fans are looking for collaborations that go beyond superficial co-branding. They want collaborations that let their favorite IPs fit naturally and meaningfully into their everyday lives. The value isn't just in owning a collectible; it's in having a piece of the world they love be part of their regular routine, whether that's a charger on their work desk or a power bank they carry every day," Cheng said.

Beyond the products themselves, fan expectations now extend to how brands participate within their communities.

According to Cheng, today's fans want brands to engage in the spaces where communities already gather, whether through conventions, fan meetups or online ecosystems. They are looking for shared experiences rather than one-way marketing campaigns.

items.title: Ugreen’s Honkai Star Rail power bank set brings gaming flair to Bangkok’s daily commute
items.summary: A new collaboration between technology accessories brand Ugreen and the hit mobile game Honkai Star Rail is turning an everyday necessity into something far more eye catching. Leading the limited edition collection is a magnetic power bank inspired by the popular character Yao Guang, combining distinctive design with practical charging performance that could prove a lifesaver for Bangkok commuters running low on battery and patience.
items.content:
A new collaboration between technology accessories brand Ugreen and the hit mobile game Honkai Star Rail is turning an everyday necessity into something far more eye catching. Leading the limited edition collection is a magnetic power bank inspired by the popular character Yao Guang, combining distinctive design with practical charging performance that could prove a lifesaver for Bangkok commuters running low on battery and patience.

Founded in Shenzhen in 2012, Ugreen has grown into a global consumer technology brand serving more than 300 million users across more than 180 countries and regions. The company has built its reputation on reliable and affordable charging products, cables, storage solutions and audio accessories that quietly keep modern life moving.

The launch comes as consumers increasingly find themselves purchasing charging accessories separately. The once familiar experience of unboxing a new smartphone complete with charger and earphones has largely disappeared. Manufacturers say the change helps reduce environmental impact, although buyers may suspect finance departments are not exactly losing sleep over the arrangement.

The result is a more demanding market, with consumers expecting faster charging, easier portability and greater convenience. Bulky chargers and tangled cables have become harder to tolerate for people juggling work, travel and social commitments throughout the day.

That is where the Honkai Star Rail collection aims to stand out. Fans of the game will instantly recognise Yao Guang, a seer strategist and general of the Xianzhou Yuque. As the game's first five star support character, she manipulates fate and grants teammates powerful extra turns. Ironically, for someone gifted with visions of the future, she still seems rather fond of a little battlefield chaos.

While gaming-themed gadgets often risk becoming little more than colourful collectibles, Ugreen's latest range offers genuine day to day usefulness.

The star attraction is undoubtedly the magnetic power bank. For commuters navigating Bangkok's BTS and MRT networks, portable charging has become almost as essential as a travel card. After all, finding a free power socket during rush hour is as unlikely as finding an empty seat.

MagFlow Air magnetic power bank Honkai: Star Rail edition

The 10,000mAh magnetic Qi2 power bank stands out for its versatile design. It combines 15W wireless charging with a built-in braided USB-C cable that doubles as a carrying strap, plus a separate USB-C port. It removes the familiar scramble through bags and backpacks when a phone battery suddenly drops into the red zone. With everything integrated into a single device, users can charge quickly without hunting for a forgotten cable. It has strong magnetic attachment, premium build quality, passthrough charging support, and the ability to charge up to 30W when using the USB-C cable instead of wireless charging.

For users spending long days away from desks and power outlets, that extra speed could make all the difference.

The power bank is a compelling alternative to competing power banks, especially because it offers both magnetic and wired charging in one compact device. While wireless charging is not the fastest available and the unit becomes warm during Qi2 charging.

The rest of the collection delivers plenty of practical appeal as well. A compact 65 watt wall charger offers fast charging for multiple devices, making it ideal for busy mornings. By the time breakfast and coffee are ready, a phone can already be significantly recharged.

Nexode retractable USB-C cable Honkai: Star Rail edition

Also included is a retractable charging cable capable of delivering up to 100 watts of power. While cables rarely generate excitement, this one earns points for avoiding the mysterious knots that somehow appear in bags and drawers despite no apparent human involvement.

items.title: Zenless Zone Zero to Get a Collaboration with Honkai: Star Rail - First Teaser Released
items.content:
1 Источник: miHoYo (HoYoverse) 17 Jul 16:04 Recently, fans of miHoYo (HoYoverse) games noticed that Pom-Pom, the conductor of the Astral Express from Honkai Star Rail, another game by the studio, appeared in the world of Zenless Zone Zero.

Now miHoYo has officially confirmed that this was intentional — there will be a full-fledged collaboration, and this is just the first teaser:

Zenless Zone Zero and Honkai: Star Rail collaboration confirmed! Hello, Proxy! We regret to inform you: based on the results of the technical evaluation, we cannot yet fix the bug with the sudden appearance of "Pom-Pombu" on Sixth Street. miHoYo published a promotional banner with the collaboration launch window in the official Zenless Zone Zero community:

The start of the Zenless Zone Zero × Honkai: Star Rail collaboration is scheduled for winter 2026. The developers have not yet revealed the details and promised to share more information in "future official announcements."

According to insider information, characters from Zenless Zone Zero will visit Honkai Star Rail. Allegedly, Astra Yao and Ellen Jo will appear in HSR 4.7; and Robin from HSR might be added to ZZZ. It is not yet clear whether they will be playable, or if it's just a cameo.

The release of Zenless Zone Zero 3.1 update is expected at the end of this month. Several new playable characters and more will be added to the game.

items.title: "Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.4 "In Ravages Does the Whistle Sound" Arrives on July 15"
items.summary: Version 4.4 gets all poetic with its "In Ravages Does the Whistle Sound" title, Asat Pramad provides an immense challenge.
items.content:
SINGAPORE, July 3, 2026 — Global interactive entertainment brand HoYoverse announced today that the brand-new Version 4.4 of Honkai: Star Rail, In Ravages Does the Whistle Sound, will launch on July 15. This version will continue the story as Planarcadia faces a crisis that threatens its survival. The Trailblazer will confront the Lord Ravager Asat Pramad and engage in an epic battle. The second phase of the Honkai: Star Rail and Fate/stay night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will also commence in this version. As another Holy Grail War begins, embark on a special chapter across the stars with Rin Tohsaka and Gilgamesh. Tap here to watch the latest trailer: https://youtu.be/xT88aPknvag Tap here to obtain the media kit: https://hoyoverse.box.com/s/lm1nq9c3od109wm31fpqnb37kwfa4kdf At the end of the previous chapter, the Lord Ravager Asat Pramad unveiled his disguise to reveal his true self and shattered the peace that had been sustained for fifteen years in Planarcadia. After the conflict broke out, Himeko vanished during her confrontation with Asat Pramad. Before she disappeared, she left behind a hidden clue related to the Express. In this version's story, the Trailblazer tracks down and deciphers the clue to locate Himeko. Asat Pramad's obsession with Himeko's identity and the truth from fifteen years ago may just be the key to unraveling his motive. Ultimately, the Trailblazer will face Asat Pramad in battle. Will Planarcadia survive this game of destruction threatening its existence? In this decisive battle, Himeko will join the fight in her new form: Himeko • Nova. The banner for the 5-star character Himeko • Nova will last throughout the entire Version 4.4. Himeko • Nova is a Fire-Type character following the Path of Erudition. When the battle begins, she immediately deploys a Territory and summons the mech "Starblazer" to assist in battle. When using her Ultimate, she leads her teammates to pilot "Starblazer" and attack enemies. When the Territory is deployed, all teammates additionally gain the Assist Skill, and they can summon "Starblazer" at any time to attack all enemies. If a teammate is part of the Express Crew, they can also gain special effects. Additionally, when using her Technique during overworld exploration, Himeko • Nova can also pilot her mech, aim at and attack enemies within range from high above in the sky. Planarcadia will also encounter an unexpected turn of events. After the end of the Fifth Holy Grail War, Rin Tohsaka embarks on a journey to another world and stumbles into Planarcadia as her magical energy runs out. In her desperation, she borrows the Holy Grail displayed as part of the Star Rail FEST collection showcase. She then attempts to summon a Servant and use the Holy Grail's power to leave this world. The overflowing Wishpower in this land restores the Holy Grail, and the King of Heroes Gilgamesh's treasures are scattered across the arcadia. A massive commotion breaks out as a result. Upon the request of the Department of Aberration Defense, the Trailblazer works with Rin Tohsaka to locate the treasures and uncover the truth behind the Imagenae: Holy Grail War. The special chapter and second phase of the Honkai: Star Rail and Fate/stay night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration officially begin on July 24. Please stay tuned. As the Holy Grail War commences once more, Rin Tohsaka joins the team as a playable character. She is a 5-star Quantum-Type character following the Path of Erudition, skilled in using gems in battle. During combat, she gains a set amount of "Gem Energy" and deals multiple additional instances of DMG to a random target by consuming the "Gem Energy" she has. The more "Gem Energy" she consumes, the more instances of additional DMG she deals. When teammates consume or recover Skill Points, CRIT DMG also increases and Rin Tohsaka accumulates "Gem Energy." Gilgamesh will also become a playable character. He is a 5-star Lightning-Type character following the Path of Destruction. After entering battle, each ally unit taking action can accumulate "Interest" for Gilgamesh, regenerate a set amount of Energy, and increase the DMG of his Ultimate. When accumulated "Interest" reaches its threshold, Gilgamesh unlocks his Skill and unleashes Gate of Babylon to fire weapons from his treasury, dealing multiple instances of DMG to enemies. When using his Ultimate, Gilgamesh summons Enuma Elish to deal massive DMG to all enemies. From the start of the collaboration on July 24 until before Version 4.6 ends, Trailblazers can log into the game and claim Gilgamesh or Archer as one of the free limited 5-star collaboration characters, along with a portion of the corresponding upgrade materials for the character. The characters and Light Cones for this collaboration will be available long term, and the guarantee counts are shared between the Collaboration Character Warps of both phases. The same applies for the Collaboration Light Cone Warps. Spend a total of 200 Star Rail Special Passes in Version 4.4 to select and claim one of the limited 5-star collaboration Light Cone "I Am As You Behold" or "The Hell Where Ideals Burn" after the collaboration begins. Limited 5-star characters Sparxie, Dan Heng • Permansor Terrae, and Evernight will return in the first half of this version for a limited time. Cerydra, Anaxa, and Aventurine will return to Warp banners in the second half of this version. During this version, Sparxie's new outfit "Candy-Coated Waves" will also be available. A new pet "Pentaflavor Emoti," Trailblaze Fashion "Fan-Made Lygus," and other new content will also be added in this version, bringing even more surprises to the journey. Lastly, Version 4.4 will also offer a variety of new events and game modes. First up, players can log in to claim a 10-pull reward once the version goes live. After the version update, the collaboration event "Fate/Star Rail Night" will also unfold as the story progresses. The Trailblazer tracks down the king's treasures with Rin Tohsaka and gradually unravels the truth behind the Imagenae: Holy Grail War. In the version event "Antigraft Brickbuster," the Trailblazer takes on a request from Aventurine and launches an investigation into IPC corruption by stacking data bricks. Additionally, the permanent gameplay feature "Currency Wars: Zero-Sum Game" will be expanded and updated. Some system features will also be optimized. Please stay tuned. Honkai: Star Rail is now available on PC, iOS, Android, Epic Games Store, and PS5™, and has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms. In 2023, the game won Apple's App Store iPhone Game of the Year, Google Play's Best Game, and BEST MOBILE GAME by The Game Awards. In 2024, it received the Golden Joystick Awards Still Playing Award (Mobile) and PlayStation® Partner Awards 2024 PARTNER AWARD among other honors. The game has been rated Teen by the ESRB and is also classified as PEGI 12. If you wish to learn more details, please visit https://hsr.hoyoverse.com or follow @HonkaiStarRail on Twitter (X), Instagram, and Facebook. About Honkai: Star Rail Honkai: Star Rail is a space fantasy RPG title with a journey through immense worlds of the unknown. The player takes on the role of "Trailblazer," a courageous individual implanted with a powerful artifact, Stellaron, and bearing the determination to unravel the mysteries surrounding the fabled "Cancer of All Worlds" and Aeons. The game features fantasy elements with myths and legends integrated into the space sci-fi story. Combined with the intuitive turn-based combat system, diverse and distinctive companions, and immersive storylines that together compose an interstellar melody filled with captivating worlds, each brimming with unique cultures, awe-inspiring landscapes, and mythical wonders to explore. About HoYoverse HoYoverse is committed to providing immersive virtual world experiences to players around the world. We have brought fans popular games including Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Honkai Impact 3rd, Tears of Themis, and Zenless Zone Zero, as well as a wide range of entertainment content. Community is at the heart of everything we do. We are devoted to engaging fans and fostering an enthusiastic and inclusive global community that provides access and encouragement for people to share their passion for ACG (Animation, Comics, and Games) through their own creativity and skills. Pushing the boundaries of imagination, we consistently explore cutting-edge game development technologies, and have accumulated leading technical capabilities in cel shading, cloud gaming, and other fields. In the future, we will continue to expand our content production, technology research, and publishing duties through operations in offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Seoul, and other areas. items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.3 guide: Events, free Jades, & banner schedule
Giving a game another chance
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it. That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I...
items.content:
Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) celebrated its three-year anniversary on April 26, 2026. I originally started playing back when it first came out, but I stopped not too long after because I didn’t really like it.

That was because I had just been playing a different game from HoYoverse, the company that makes HSR, that I had to stop playing because of bugs. I also stopped because it was really laggy, but I realized when I started playing again this past December that I had actually originally played on the European server rather than the American one, which was why it was lagging.

Now that I’ve started playing it again for the last four months, I’m wishing I’d never quit.

The game’s story is amazing. With games like HSR where the main character is a self-insert, I tend to fully lean into that role. As such, whenever a major twist happens to a character that the main character has bonded with, I really feel it due to the immersion.

Another thing I like about the story is that HSR keeps you on your toes because it isn’t afraid to kill off playable characters.

I’d played a different game from HoYoverse before HSR, and it wouldn’t dream of killing a playable character, so I went into HSR thinking it’d be the same. That idea went out the window on my second day of playing with the first of many playable character deaths.

Because of that, you end up wanting to make sure you own your favorite characters in case you never see them in the game again. However, since HSR is a gacha game, you’re not guaranteed to get the characters you want when they’re available without spending money.

At least that’s what you’d think, but from my experience, HSR is the easiest gacha game I’ve played when it comes to getting the characters you want without spending money.

I’ve managed to get three characters I’ve wanted along with two of their exclusive items without spending money. That’s because HSR makes it really easy to get the in-game currency for pulling characters. That means if you just want to get a character for the sake of having them, you can.

In fact, I’d say HSR is probably the only gacha game where you don’t have to spend real money. I only spent money on cosmetics, but most cosmetics are free rewards from permanent events.

The only negative thing I have to say about the game is that the newer main quests are fairly long.

The latest finished questline takes 62 hours to complete, and the entire main quest line is currently over 100 hours. Because of that, if you have a busy daily schedule, it could take a while to complete. It is possible to finish in a week, but based on personal experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

The length aside, I would highly recommend this game, especially since it’s free on PC and you don’t even need a gaming one as I play on my laptop. With the three years of content in the game so far, I can’t wait to see where it goes from here.

items.title: MAPPA, HoYoverse Release 'Animation Concept Trailer' for Honkai: Star Rail Game (Updated)
items.content:
HoYoverse revealed during a livestream for its Honkai: Star Rail game on Friday that it and MAPPA have co-produced an "animation concept trailer" for the game. The trailer, viewable below, is titled "Death in the Afternoon."

Yuzuru Tachikawa ( Mob Psycho 100 , Death Parade director) directed the trailer and Kayoko Ishikawa ( Sarazanmai , ZENSHU. ) was the character designer. The end of the above video features the words " MAPPA Honkai: Star Rail Animation A New Story Awaits."

The HoYoverse staff had introduced the video in the livestream as a "mysterious collaboration project." HoYoverse's press release about the livestream announcements stated that at the end of the livestream, "...the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, 'Death in the Afternoon.' Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures!"

The livestream and HoYoverse's press release did not give any further details. It is currently unclear if the "original animation project" is the above trailer, or if the collaboration will include other works.

Update: ANN reached out to HoYoverse for clarification, and the company provided the following response:

HoYoverse launched its Honkai: Star Rail game for PC and mobile in April 2023, and then for PlayStation 5 in October 2023. The game has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms.

The game will launch its Version 4.2 patch on April 22. The patch will celebrate the game's third anniversary.

HoYoverse's earlier game Genshin Impact launched a "long-term collaboration project" with ufotable in 2022. The project is still in production.

items.title: Hands on with the Honkai: Star Rail v4.0 experience
items.summary: This HoyoVerse train just keeps on chugging!
items.content:
The last article I wrote for Honkai: Star Rail was going over the details of the upcoming Version 4.0 release . Since then, HoYoverse generously offered up the opportunity to play Version 4.0 and experience Planarcadia early. Having spent about a dozen hours or so playing with the new characters, experiencing the story, and generally taking in the sights and sounds of Planarcadia, I’m prepared to share my thoughts on all of it.

It’s best to start off with the main attraction of Version 4.0: Planarcadia. This new planet is a fictional world come to life and boy does it leave a fantastic first impression. Full of the kind of sights and sounds you’d expect from an Asian city brimming with life. Exploration is a blast with all the alleys and little nooks to find, the platforming segments that can either help you navigate across certain parts of the city or find chests within them. There’s also a new style of puzzles that require you to rotate a 2D plane in a 3D space to “paint” certain parts of it to make them solid and let you platform with those objects. Planarcadia is so full of whimsy and still has some of the overhang of a crime family really enabling a super unique feeling planet compared to what we’ve had with previous locations such as the Xianzhou or Amphoreus.

The two new characters following the path of Elation feel great, even if the Aha Moment is a little overstimulating sometimes. Sparxie and Yao Guang fit on a team together like a glove to demolish all the bosses I’ve thrown them against. I’m eager to see where the new path goes with time, especially since we only have the two characters currently. Even as of the live public server branch, we’re unsure when Elation Trailblazer will make their debut, so keep an eye on that as versions progress beyond 4.0. You’ll need to get a hold of new Elation Light Cones as well since they obviously can’t use the other Paths’ options. Burning skill points to increase the Elation stacks until Aha decides he’s satisfied and steps in for a big attack feels really great and it has me curious what future Elation characters might do when they trigger their own Aha Moments.

Not to mention that for new players, you’ve got the opportunity to really kickstart a team of your choice with a new planet. We’re at a point in the game where there’s so many options for characters you can pick from and build around, and 4.0 introducing Elation means that as a new player, you can jump in and get a headstart on pulling for that archetype. Especially with a new Novaflare round of buffs, there’s even more options than before bringing older characters back into the limelight. The Black Swan and Sparkle buffs are so massive that people running DoT teams or any team using an action advance support such as Bronya or Sunday have another insane option. Sparkle was always good, but her Novaflare enables her to further buff your DPS units to extreme levels. Black Swan’s Novaflare was even more insane and rocketed her back up to the top for damage even as a DoT unit. Combined with the option to pick a free character including units like Sparkle, Kafka (who works great in DoT teams), and more, you really can’t go wrong in Planarcadia and the Version 4.0 patch from what I’ve gotten to experience.

Between the free characters, the great change of pace in the story from the latter half of Amphoreus (if you’ve played it, you know), the new cityscape that is quite honestly my new favorite location in the game, and all the new characters to look forward to, you really should make a return to Star Rail if you’ve been away for a minute and are curious about where we’re at. If you’re new, definitely consider giving it a shot. There’s even a bonus to let you convert trace materials for leveling character skills at a 1 to 1 ratio this time instead of a 2 for 1, so you really can kickstart your Elation team. With characters being important again like Silver Wolf, Blade, and Himeko, as well as new faces like Sparxie, Yao Guang, Ashveil, and Pearl, I think 4.0 is just the start of a real treat of a patch cycle for Honkai: Star Rail.

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.0 impressions
items.content:
I'll admit, I recently burned out on Honkai: Star Rail. Upon hearing the news that 3.8 would be the lengthiest patch yet and with content more sparse than ever before, I decided to take a break for the first time since I started playing all the way back in 1.0. The entire Amphoreus saga left me feeling drained; I thoroughly enjoyed 3.0-3.4 as excellent set-up chapters, but felt lost as the plot became a labyrinth of hidden motivations, layered twists, hours of exposition, and endless proper nouns. When looking at the story as a whole, I love the characters (Aglaea and Anaxa in particular) and the rich history of the world within the Scepter, but the later patches often felt like studying for a needlessly convoluted test. I understood the gist of what was happening, but I won't lie to you and say I could describe to you in detail what Cyrene's deal is or how Evernight fits into everything.

All that's to say: I was looking forward to the Astral Express crew taking a well-earned vacation to Planarcadia, the planet of Elation. Despite two of the game's four current versions ostensibly beginning with Akivili's disciples deciding that they need a break from the backbreaking work of saving the universe, neither has resulted in our trailblazers seeing much downtime. Unlike previous excursions, it's all hands on deck: everyone gets off at this stop (save for Black Swan's incredibly hasty and unfortunate exit prior to departure). It's fun to see the entire main cast get involved, none more welcome than Himeko — up until now, the only character trait I could've told you about her was that she's terrible at making coffee. Getting some elaboration on her backstory and giving her a personality outside of "Express mom" is long overdue.

The Trailblazer and March 7th begin their Planarcadian getaway with a suitably devious greeting by none other than our old pal Sparkle. We're given a tour of the vibrant, totally-not-Japanese-inspired streets, crawling with humans living in tentative harmony with totally-not-Penaconian-memetic-entities known as imagenae. Here, we catch a glimpse of what I hope will become one of Planarcadia's core themes: gentrification and the plight of capitalism, with a side of anti-imperialism (all perpetrated by the IPC, of course). It's bold, though, and I worry that future patches will keep these criticisms in the background rather than highlight them as Planarcadia's core issues. I would love so much for little nuggets of lore to be elaborated upon, ones that suggest a more serious political history than Aha would have you believe: what did the imagenae do before the IPC forced them to integrate into society? Were they not allowed to work at all? Were they marginalized and seen as second-class citizens? Is the Department of Aberration Defense an inherently evil organization left to determine on their own which imagenae deserve their continued existence and which do not? Is Kuchiba so hot that it doesn't even matter?

This brings us to the Synwish Syndicate, a gang formerly designed to be a respite for imagenae that feel rejected elsewhere, now, due to IPC intervention, a gang that largely exists to enable monetary gain by questionable means. Here at the syndicate's headquarters, the plot quickly begins to balloon into what feels like a collection of introductions for what's to come. We have Pearl's cold and calculating grip on the planet, Himeko and her confounding family history, the potential return of the Herald of Death, the Stellaron Hunters' unknown involvement in the Phantasmoon Games, Sunday's inadvertent entry into the Games, Evanescia's whole...thing, and Yao Guang's bottomless supply of divinations. What's most shocking is that the patch still manages to pull off a fun (if bloated) self-contained story, adding layers to one of HSR's most inscrutable characters and ending things with one of the game's best low-stakes twists.

I'm no Xianzhou Arbiter-General, but I can pretty easily peer into the future and divine a prophecy for Honkai: Star Rail: each new patch will introduce and/or discuss at length a new prophecy that cryptically divulges the fate of a character and/or planet and/or simulation masquerading as a planet. It's hard to pinpoint the moment a theme becomes a crutch, but I think HSR passed that moment long ago. In this patch, we have not one, not two, but three central characters that are defined by their relationship with prophecy and prediction — Yao Guang, Pearl, and the perennial mystery that is Elio and his script. So many in-game conversations devolve into the interpretation of prophecy, and frankly, it's becoming exhausting. We went through an entire version in which each Chrysos Heir had a poetically vague predetermined fate, and before that (and in 3.8's ret-con-y confusion) we had Sparkle's ambiguous "three deaths" for Firefly.

If this were a wholesale replacement for well-executed foreshadowing, we would have a far bigger issue. It's obvious, though, that the writing team knows how to tell a story sans-prophecy, evident in Sparkle's character-driven narrative in this very patch. Sparxie being the "true" Sparkle (as much as old Sparkle is also the "true" Sparkle) is teased so perfectly; the reveal is obvious in retrospect while being difficult to predict with the given information. It's consistently groan-inducing to see this writing cheat code being used ad nauseam within a story that could function better without it. I hope I'll be proven wrong and the game will subvert the words of its murky prophets, leaving me with egg on my face come the conclusion of this leg of the Express' journey.

4.0 is a promising new beginning, and has at the very least brought me back in terms of its story. Though there is an abundance of new proper nouns to memorize and a bevy of new and returning cast members to keep track of, the patch still takes on a welcome return to simplicity and levity (save for the shocking tonal shift right at the end, RIP the Synwish Syndicate Feb. 2026 - Feb. 2026). As long as things don't get too bogged down in extensive metaphors and tiresome exposition, I'm hopeful that Planarcadia can become the most focused version of HSR we've seen so far.
